contribution: A Macedonian general, regent and statesman under the successive kingships of Philip II of Macedon and his son, Alexander the Great.

checks.lead: Antipater ( ; Ancient Greek: Ἀντίπατρος, romanized: Antipatros, lit. 'like the father'; c. 400 BC – 319 BC) was a Macedonian general, regent and statesman under the successive kingships of Philip II of Macedon and his son, Alexander the Great. In the wake of the collapse of the Argead house, his son Cassander eventually ruled Macedonia as a king in his own right.
